event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: The filing—dated February 15 2022, i.e., within two years of the WHO’s March 11 2020 pandemic declaration—contains an extensive, dedicated COVID-19 risk discussion.  The language is mostly recent-impact and forward-looking, not hypothetical: management cites concrete disruptions already experienced (lower demand, supply-chain delays, remote-work complications) and explicitly warns of material adverse effects on revenue, cash-flows and operations if conditions persist or worsen.  The disclosures also detail sector-specific pressures (livestock plant shutdowns, labor shortages, vaccination-mandate uncertainty) that could structurally affect Zoetis’ markets.  Although no hard dollar figure is provided, the statements are highly specific, cover multiple operational vectors (supply, demand, workforce, regulation), and acknowledge continuing uncertainty through 2022.  Under the Time-Decay Principle, a pandemic still unfolding (0-3 years) justifies high severity scores (7-9) where direct impacts are described, with moderate scores (3-6) for secondary or less-quantified effects, and minor deductions where mitigation or uncertainty is emphasised.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has negatively affected the global economy; has disrupted our and our customers', suppliers', and vendors' operations; has negatively affected certain elements of our business and operations; and may materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or cash flows.

components.reason: States concrete disruptions across the entire value chain.
Explicitly warns of ‘materially adversely affect’ on financial metrics.
Covers both current impacts and future risk (‘has’ and ‘may’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct admission of present and potential material harm across operations and finances warrants a high score of 8.

evidence_list.snippet: The global spread of COVID-19 has had, and may continue to have, an adverse impact on our operations, sales and delivery and supply chains.

components.reason: Links pandemic to operations, sales and supply chain—core business functions.
Notes continuing nature (‘may continue to have’).
No mitigating language offered.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad, ongoing adverse impact across critical functions merits a strong risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has and may continue to impact our supply chain as we experience disruptions or delays in shipments of certain materials or components of our products.

components.reason: Specifies supply-chain disruptions and shipment delays.
Highlights persistence (‘has and may continue’).
Direct link to product availability.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific, ongoing supply-chain risk justifies a score at the higher end of the range.

evidence_list.snippet: Any prolonged component shortages or supply chain disruption may result in manufacturing or R&D delays and could limit our ability to meet customer demand or otherwise adversely impact our revenue, and may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or cash flows.

components.reason: Connects shortages to manufacturing/R&D delays and unmet demand.
Points to revenue impact and broader material adverse effect.
Conditional but clearly severe if prolonged.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Describes cascading operational delays leading to revenue harm; severity balanced by conditional language.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic also has and may continue to reduce demand for some of our products as a result of the negative impact it has had and may continue to have on our customers.

components.reason: Mentions actual and continuing reduction in product demand.
Ties weakness to customer difficulties, signalling systemic risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Demand erosion is significant though less quantified, yielding a solid but slightly lower score.

evidence_list.snippet: In particular, our livestock customers have been and may continue to be challenged by voluntary or mandatory facility closures, reduced packing plant capacity, travel bans and quarantines inhibiting consumption of protein and transportation of live animals, and labor shortages negatively impacting their operations.

components.reason: Enumerates specific operational obstacles for key customer segment.
Indicates both current and future persistence.
Details multiple external constraints (closures, capacity, labor).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Customer-side operational disruptions threaten sales indirectly; detailed but customer-specific, so moderate-high score.

evidence_list.snippet: The resulting reduction in demand for some of our products has negatively impacted our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows and may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or cash flows, if such demand reduction accelerates or is prolonged.

components.reason: Confirms realized negative impact on financial metrics.
Warns of future material adverse effect if trend persists.
Highlights potential escalation (‘accelerates or is prolonged’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Actual financial harm plus warning of worsening conditions earns a high risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: Additionally, many of our workforce continue to work remotely as a result of the pandemic.

components.reason: Identifies operational change (remote work) directly attributable to COVID-19.
Indicates ongoing status (‘continue to’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Remote-work fact signals operational shift but without quantified harm, resulting in a lower relative score.

evidence_list.snippet: Remote working arrangements could result in additional complexity or inefficiency or increase operational risks, including, but not limited to, risks associated with information technology and systems which could have a material adverse effect on our business.

components.reason: Links remote work to increased complexity and IT risks.
States possibility of material adverse effect.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specifies operational and IT risk path; important but less immediate than supply/demand shocks.

evidence_list.snippet: While it is not currently possible to predict with any certainty the exact impact the new regulations would have on us, our suppliers and our customers, the implementation of such government mandated vaccination or testing mandates may impact our ability to retain current employees and attract new employees and result in labor disruptions.

components.reason: Flags regulatory (vaccine/testing mandates) risk leading to labor disruption.
Acknowledges uncertainty, slightly mitigating severity.
Covers potential impact on suppliers and customers as well.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Regulatory-driven labor risk is notable but tempered by acknowledged uncertainty.

evidence_list.snippet: We cannot at this time predict the full impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, but we anticipate that the COVID-19 pandemic is likely to continue to impact our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or cash flows in 2022.

components.reason: Projects continued impact through current fiscal year.
Admits inability to quantify—a partial mitigating factor.
Covers broad financial dimensions (business, financial condition, results, cash flows).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking statement underscores persistence of risk though lacking specifics, producing a mid-range score.
